clue.text: Man of note, heartbroken

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the word before are reassembled

explanation.surface: A man known for his music has been left heartbroken.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, Welsh in origin, so it stands for a male person.

clue.text: Moslem prince heard announcing 'is presence

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is spoken, and the spelling entered differs from the spoken words

parts.note: a Cockney announcing his own presence says "am 'ere" (I am here), with the h dropped

explanation.surface: A Muslim prince is heard proclaiming that he has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''is' signals a dropped h, so the speech is Cockney: "am 'ere" for "am here".
explanation.definitionFit: An emir, a ruler or prince in Muslim lands, also spelt with a double E.

clue.text: Mixture of toddy seen to be avoided by seamen

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters of the next two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Sailors should keep away from a blend of hot toddy, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eddystone Rocks off Plymouth are a notorious hazard to shipping, marked by a famous lighthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef in the English Channel that ships must steer clear of.

clue.text: Hamlet's mobled queen

parts.note: in Shakespeare's play, the Player recites a speech about the muffled-faced queen of Troy weeping for Priam

explanation.surface: A quotation recalling a muffled queen from Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The mobled queen' is Hamlet's own phrase in Act 2; 'mobled' means with head and face muffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam's wife, queen of Troy, whose grief is described in the Player's speech.

clue.text: Hunt's left?

parts.note: read as a hunting call: the cry raised when the fox has broken cover and the field sets off

explanation.surface: Has the hunt already departed?
explanation.walkthrough: In British foxhunting, the huntsman's cry when the fox leaves cover is a set two-word call, which also means simply 'departed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunting cry that the quarry has left cover; literally, departed.

clue.text: Novel way Dowson's memories were blown away

definitions.meaning: Margaret Mitchell's 1936 novel of the American Civil War

definitions.text: way Dowson's memories were blown away
definitions.meaning: Ernest Dowson's poem Cynara says 'I have forgot much, Cynara!' and that things went with the wind

explanation.surface: A poet's recollections scattered as if by a strong breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Mitchell took her title from Dowson's line, so both definitions point to one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Mitchell's famous book title, borrowed from a line in Dowson's poem about lost memories.

clue.text: Airways may be stopped by cold conditions

definitions.text: Airways may be stopped by cold conditions

parts.words: Airways may be stopped by cold conditions
parts.note: airways read not as airlines halted by weather but as the passages of the nose, blocked up when one has a cold

explanation.surface: Flights may be grounded by wintry weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airways' and 'cold conditions' suggest airlines and freezing weather; the real picture is a blocked nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The nasal openings through which we breathe, which get stuffed up with a cold.

clue.text: Delicacy like one swallowed by Bobby

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside the word that follows

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, PC for police constable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something tasty, like one item gulped down by a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury jelly, regarded as a fine dish.

clue.text: To the Parisian, and to many pests, they appear dictatorial

parts.note: au is French for to the
C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number
rats are pests

explanation.surface: A Frenchman thinks many vermin behave like tyrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute rulers, who by nature behave in a dictatorial manner.

clue.text: Beggars, for instance -five hundred thousand, roughly

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000

indicators.note: roughly suggests an inexact, rearranged version of the letters gathered

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: There are, for example, about half a million beggars.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicants are those who live by begging, such as begging friars.

clue.text: Much money in these Burslem products

definitions.meaning: ... of money means a great deal of it
Burslem is one of the Potteries towns of Stoke-on-Trent, famous for ceramics

explanation.surface: There is a lot of cash to be made from Staffordshire wares.
explanation.walkthrough: Burslem, in the English Potteries district, is the 'mother town' of the pottery industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a large sum of money, and ceramic vessels made in the Potteries.

clue.text: Go over the front of the ship with a weapon

parts.note: to cross is to go over
the bow is the forward end of a ship

explanation.surface: Climb across the prow of the vessel carrying arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical bow mounted on a stock, used to shoot bolts.

clue.text: Fabulous bird — coo! Crazy style!

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of legend

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of the exclamation are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An excited cry at a mythical bird done in an outlandish manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The text held 'too!' where the page prints 'coo!'. 'Crazy' turns COO into OCO.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornate eighteenth-century decorative style, full of curves and scrollwork.

clue.text: Vivacity in the bar: it's that b--- port !

parts.note: a censored swear word beginning with b, standing for its first letter
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Liveliness in a pub as someone curses that wretched harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes print an expletive as its initial only, so it gives just B.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is liveliness and spirit, especially in performance.

clue.text: How we were caught with a fistful of diamonds ?

definitions.text: How we were caught with a fistful of diamonds ?

parts.words: How we were caught with a fistful of diamonds ?
parts.note: diamonds read as the red card suit, so a hand full of them is literally coloured red, as well as caught in the act of theft

explanation.surface: We were nabbed holding stolen gems.
explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds suggest stolen jewels, but in cards they are a red suit, so a hand full of them is literally a red hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in the act of wrongdoing, as if with blood still on one's hands.

clue.text: Charm of Dutch navigator when about 51

indicators.note: about means the navigator's name goes around the number

parts.note: Abel Tasman was the Dutch explorer who reached Tasmania and New Zealand
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The lucky piece belonged to a Dutch explorer from around fifty years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object believed to bring luck or ward off harm, an amulet.

clue.text: Periodical seen on the stand ?

definitions.meaning: the ..., a long-running British weekly magazine
one watching from a grandstand at a sporting event

explanation.surface: A magazine displayed on a newsstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' suggests a news-stand for the magazine; the second sense is a spectator in the grandstand.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known weekly journal, and an onlooker in the stands.

clue.text: Highly respectful, always put up with landlord's demand

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ever means always
rent is what a landlord asks of a tenant

explanation.surface: A very deferential tenant has always tolerated the landlord's charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate; 'put up' alone turns EVER upward into REVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deep respect or veneration.

clue.text: Follower might be a backward mug?

definitions.text: Follower might be a backward mug?

parts.words: Follower might be a backward mug?
parts.note: a follower is one who sticks to a cause; a mug or sucker clings fast, and a backward one hangs on behind

explanation.surface: A disciple could be a slow-witted fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' suggests a fool; read it as a sucker that clings, so a follower is one who sticks behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or follower, literally one who sticks to someone.

clue.text: Mysterious second news item ?

definitions.meaning: the 'mysterious ...' is a stock phrase for the Orient
the compass points N, E, W, S spell news, and the second of them is this one

explanation.surface: An enigmatic follow-up story in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News item' suggests a press story; the item is the second letter-point of N-E-W-S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient, proverbially mysterious, and the compass point second in N-E-W-S.

clue.text: Indian servant shows endurance ?

definitions.meaning: in British India a ... was a household servant
one who bears, that is endures, hardship

explanation.surface: A domestic servant in India puts up with a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal servant in colonial India, and one who bears or endures.

clue.text: .He aims, to reorganize the club

indicators.note: reorganizing means rearranging, so the letters of the two words before are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man is planning a shake-up of the society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a society; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned golf club, roughly a five-iron.

clue.text: Rustic upstart joins man of religion

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer
read as up-start, the starting letter of up

explanation.surface: An ambitious peasant joins the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstart' looks like a social climber; read as up's start it gives U.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Hinduism, a man of that faith.

clue.text: After 25, goodbye to these animals

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, the garden of Genesis
ta-ta is a casual goodbye

explanation.surface: After the garden, farewell to these creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The order of mammals with few or no teeth, such as sloths and anteaters.

clue.text: Dwarf has to walk without leader

indicators.note: without leader means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a stroll is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: A small person must go on foot without anyone in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is a Scandinavian goblin, often pictured as a dwarf.

clue.text: Some weed engulfing the garden?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A weed taking over the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden of Adam and Eve, the archetypal garden.

clue.text: Oriental fighter gets a share on leaving the country

parts.note: E for east, the Orient
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: An Eastern warrior receives his portion when he departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigration is departure from one's homeland to settle abroad.

clue.text: Regulated only in the case of dead letters

indicators.note: in the case of means placed inside a covering made of the other part
the letters of the word are taken loose and rearranged

parts.note: just means only

explanation.surface: Rules applied solely to undeliverable mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead letters' suggests undeliverable mail; 'letters' here jumbles DEAD into ADED, which encases JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted means set or regulated to the correct level.

clue.text: Are many employed in transport.? Not often

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Do lots of people work on the railways? Seldom.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, on few occasions.
